Requirement: The system shall record, as a committed fail-closed receipt, that the host drove the reviewer VM's Copilot agent to run the RELEASED net-only lbabus (collab-cli 0.15.0, pulled from the immutable collab-cli-v0.15.0 release) and the VM reported task-correlated results back over the lbabus net TCP bus -- the sole coordination path, since the released CLI rejects the retired init/post/poll/wait/delta Discussion commands -- so a fail-closed gate proves the end-to-end net-only drive loop is reproducible off any GitHub-Discussion dependency.
Notes: ADR-0049 net-only live VM-agent drive: builds on the read-back mechanism of LBA-REQ-059/ADR-0039 but proves the loop with the RELEASED net-only binary (collab-cli-v0.15.0) installed on the reviewer VM. The committed net-only-live-drive-receipt@1 seals 3 real drives from the VM (senderId WIN, matched over lbabus net TCP): net-only install, benchmark re-drive (launch-to-ready 2604.2 ms/5 samples PASS), and the WIN 0.15.0 release sign-off (version=0.15.0, post=unknown command exit 1, PASS); plus the net-only CLI proof (collab-cli-v0.15.0 rejects init/post/poll/wait/delta). The verifier (net-only-live-drive.mjs) re-derives the digest + verdict deterministically + fails closed on a non-WIN/unmatched drive, an incomplete net-only proof, a forged verdict, or a tampered digest; selftest 7/7; gate net-only-live-drive. Comms-only (ADR-0003): each reply is a one-line status.

Requirement: The system shall record, as a committed fail-closed receipt, that ONE release-with-review loop is bound to a single candidate over the net-only bus -- the reviewer VM staged the candidate over lbabus net, a human Ed25519-signed a visual PASS/FAIL of THAT candidate (component/version/commit/vsixSha256), and the signed verdict announced over net with its semantic type -- so a fail-closed gate proves the staged, signed, and announced candidate are the SAME.
Notes: ADR-0050 release-with-review drive: binds the net-staged candidate (LBA-REQ-068) to the signed visual verdict (LBA-REQ-057) announced over net (LBA-REQ-058) -- all bound to the same candidate. The verifier release-with-review-drive.mjs REUSES verifyReviewerVerdict/gateVisualReview/buildVerdictBusPost from reviewerVerdict.mjs + adds the binding: a matched WIN staging drive over net, the verdict target == the staged candidate (component/version/commit/vsixSha256), the enrolled Ed25519 sign-off verifies + the visual-review gate publishes, and the net announce is correctly derived (type/task/ref). The committed release-with-review-drive-receipt@1 seals one real round (ext 0.5.0 staged over net task rev-1785753563, signed PASS by reviewer@vi-tech.nl, announced RESOLVED on extension-release-0.5.0); re-derives the binding + verdict + digest deterministically + fails closed on a candidate mismatch, an unverified sign-off, a non-publishing gate, a mis-derived announce, or a tampered digest; selftest 7/7; gate release-with-review-drive. Comms-only (ADR-0003).

Requirement: The system shall record, as a committed fail-closed receipt, that a release candidate publishes ONLY when BOTH the machine corroboration gate (a quorum verdict + an enrolled sign-off over it, ADR-0018) AND the human visual gate (an enrolled signed PASS of the built candidate, LBA-REQ-057) pass, AND both name the SAME net-staged candidate (LBA-REQ-068/069) -- so a fail-closed gate proves the machine quorum, the human visual verdict, and the net stage all name one candidate.
Notes: ADR-0051 composite release decision (capstone): binds the machine corroboration gate (gateReleasePublish, ADR-0018/LBA-REQ-027) to the human visual gate (gateVisualReview, LBA-REQ-057) over the SAME net-staged candidate (LBA-REQ-068/069). The verifier composite-release-decision.mjs REUSES gateReleaseWithReview (which composes gateReleasePublish + gateVisualReview) + candidatesMatch/stagedOk + adds the cross-gate binding: the machine quorum consensus.version/sourceCommit == the candidate == the visual verdict target, and the candidate was staged over net by a matched WIN drive. The committed composite-release-decision-receipt@1 seals one real round (ext 0.5.0: passing 2-witness quorum + an enrolled sign-off over the quorum digest + an enrolled signed visual PASS + the net staging drive rev-1785753563), one reviewer signing both gates with one enrolled Ed25519 key; re-derives the decision + binding + digest deterministically + fails closed unless both gates publish AND both name the staged candidate (or on a tampered digest); selftest 7/7; gate composite-release-decision. No gate reinvented. Comms-only (ADR-0003).

Requirement: The extension release workflow shall block publishing a .vsix unless a committed composite release-decision proves BOTH gates pass for the tagged candidate version -- the agreement job runs verify-composite-release.mjs (fail-closed) and the publish release job depends on agreement -- so no extension release publishes without the bound composite decision (LBA-REQ-070).
Notes: ADR-0052 enforce the composite release decision: verify-composite-release.mjs REUSES the gated composite validateReceipt (LBA-REQ-070) to require the committed composite receipt to name the tagged <component,version> + be proven (exit 0 clear / 1 fail-closed); extension-release.yml's agreement job runs it after verify-visual-review, and the release (publish) job needs [build, agreement], so the composite decision GATES the publish. The gate composite-release-enforced proves (offline, deterministic) the CLI clears ext 0.5.0 + fails closed for a version with no proven decision, and that extension-release.yml wires the CLI in the publish-gating agreement job. Completes the release-gate arc: machine quorum (027) + human visual (057) + net stage (068) + stage-sign-announce binding (069) + machine+human composite (070) + the enforced publish gate (071). Only runs on ext-v* tags / workflow_dispatch (not PR CI); a future release adds its own composite receipt.

Requirement: The system shall prove that a Linux and a Windows launch-to-ready benchmark receipt measure the SAME benchmark via a machine-independent launch identity (metric + workload + sample count) -- so their plane-specific timings are legitimately comparable -- and a fail-closed gate rejects an identity mismatch, a non-cross-plane pair, or a tampered receipt.
Notes: ADR-0053 cross-plane launch-benchmark parity: the flagship exact-12-FPS launch-to-ready benchmark measures a plane-DEPENDENT quantity (~2604 ms Linux vs ~2410 ms Windows), so its cross-plane identity is the benchmark SPEC not the series (unlike mprr seriesHash LBA-REQ-014 / VI Analyzer resultHash LBA-REQ-015/043). launchParity.mjs launchIdentity = sha256 over {metric,workload,n}; parity proven iff both are valid workload-trend@1, cross-plane (one LINUX + one WIN), identities match; the plane means + signed delta + faster plane are performance witnesses, not identity. The committed cross-plane-launch-parity-receipt@1 is DERIVED FROM the committed launch-trend fixtures (experiments/launch-parity/fixtures/{linux,win}-launch-trend.json) -- LINUX 2604.2 ms vs WIN 2410.6 ms, WIN faster by 193.6 ms (-7.4%); the gate re-derives it + asserts it reflects the real trend means (non-fabricable). Fails closed on identity mismatch / non-cross-plane / invalid trend / tampered digest; selftest 7/7; gate cross-plane-launch-parity. Realizes the roadmap Phase 2/4 parity metric for the flagship benchmark.

Requirement: The system shall prove fulfillment of a DISPATCHED cross-plane benchmark run by validating that >= N distinct enrolled mesh actors from the requested planes each returned a valid plane-tagged receipt for the SAME benchmark identity -- so a fail-closed gate proves the mesh run was fulfilled by enough independent cross-plane actors, with no central results database (the returned receipts ARE the result).
Notes: ADR-0054 mesh-run cross-plane fulfillment (roadmap Phase 3, the North Star loop): a dispatched cross-plane benchmark run is proven fulfilled by >= N independent enrolled actors from distinct planes, each returning a valid plane-tagged receipt for the SAME benchmark identity -- no central DB, the receipts ARE the result. meshFulfillment.mjs REUSES the LBA-REQ-072 launchIdentity as the cross-actor agreement invariant + composes the actor identity (LBA-REQ-039) + the provider-delegation CLAIM/ACK/DONE dispatch primitives (LBA-REQ-018). Fulfilled iff >= minActors distinct actors, requested planes covered, each a valid plane-tagged workload-trend@1 (plane matches actor), all identities agree; fails closed on too few/duplicate/uncovered-plane/invalid/identity-disagreement/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7); gate mesh-run-cross-plane-fulfillment. The committed mesh-run-fulfillment-receipt@1 seals a REAL run: labview-ide-launch fulfilled by golden-linux (LINUX 2604.2 ms) + golden-win (WIN 2410.6 ms), each embedding its real launch-trend receipt. Realizes the section-8 mesh metric. Next Phase-3 increment: the repository_dispatch transport.

Requirement: The system shall dispatch a cross-plane benchmark run GitHub-natively via a repository_dispatch event carrying a validated mesh-run-dispatch@1 request bound to its fulfillment, and gate the returned receipts on cross-plane fulfillment -- so a fail-closed gate proves the dispatch->fulfill loop is wired with no central server (the repo IS the queue).
Notes: ADR-0055 GitHub-native mesh-run dispatch transport (roadmap Phase 3): closes the dispatch->fulfill loop. meshDispatch.mjs validates a mesh-run-dispatch@1 request (benchmarkId + {metric,workload,n} spec + minActors>=1 + non-empty valid requestedPlanes + dispatchId), carrying the LBA-REQ-072 launchIdentity so a dispatch + its fulfillment (LBA-REQ-073) are provably the SAME run; fails closed on missing-benchmarkId/bad-minActors/empty-or-invalid-planes/identity-mismatch/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml triggers on repository_dispatch[mesh-run] (the client_payload IS the request; the repo IS the queue), validates the dispatch, then gates the returned receipts with meshFulfillment (no central DB). Gate mesh-run-dispatch-wired proves offline: the committed request validates + BINDS to the LBA-REQ-073 fulfillment (same benchmarkId + identity + minActors + planes) + mesh-run.yml is wired (repository_dispatch[mesh-run] + both verifiers). Live fan-out (actor tasking + receipt-collection artifacts) is the next Phase-3 increment.

Requirement: The system shall fold the governed mesh-run receipts (dispatch, fulfillment, cross-plane parity) into a coverage matrix + a consistency ledger -- which benchmarks x which planes x how many actors fulfilled, and whether each run's dispatch/fulfillment/parity name the SAME identity -- so a fail-closed gate proves the operator-facing mesh dashboard reflects the receipts it summarizes.
Notes: ADR-0056 the mesh coverage observatory (roadmap Phase 3->4): folds the governed mesh-run receipts (dispatch LBA-REQ-074 + fulfillment LBA-REQ-073 + cross-plane parity LBA-REQ-072) into a mesh-coverage-observatory@1 coverage matrix + consistency ledger -- benchmarks x planes x actors, and whether each run's dispatch/fulfillment/parity name the SAME identity. meshObservatory.mjs folds each run into a coverage row (dispatched, fulfilled, distinct actors, covered planes, parity proven, consistent) + derives the matrix + ledger; fails closed on identity-disagreement/un-fulfilled-counted-coherent/miscounted-coverage/stale-re-fold/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). The committed observatory re-derives byte-stably from the committed source receipts (currency) + is grounded in the real LBA-REQ-073 fulfillment (identity + actor count + covered planes). Gate mesh-coverage-observatory. The operator-facing mesh dashboard + the Phase 3->4 cross-plane-comparison-at-scale bridge; folding more fulfilled runs extends the matrix with no new machinery.

Requirement: The system shall expand a validated mesh-run dispatch into per-plane actor tasking and validate the returned-receipt collection that feeds fulfillment, both identity-bound to the dispatch -- so a fail-closed gate proves every collected receipt provably descends from the dispatched tasks and ran the SAME benchmark.
Notes: ADR-0057 the live fan-out contract (roadmap Phase 3): governs the two contracts BETWEEN dispatch (LBA-REQ-074) + fulfillment (LBA-REQ-073) -- how a dispatch TASKS actors (actor-tasking@1) + how their returned receipts are COLLECTED back into the fulfillment input (receipt-collection@1), both identity-bound to the dispatch via the LBA-REQ-072 launchIdentity. meshFanout.mjs derives one identity-bound task per requested plane + validates a collection mapping each returned receipt to its task; fails closed on unbound-task/uncovered-plane/no-matching-task/plane-or-identity-mismatch/duplicate-actor/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). The committed tasking re-derives from the committed dispatch (currency) + the collection reconstructs the committed LBA-REQ-073 fulfillment (grounding: the collected set IS the fulfillment actor set). .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml runs the fan-out step between validating the dispatch + gating fulfillment. Gate mesh-live-fanout-wired. Wiring live actor execution slots into the collection contract with no new governance.

Requirement: The system shall admit a returned mesh-actor receipt into a verified collection only when it carries a valid attestation from its declared, enrolled actor -- so a fail-closed gate proves each collected receipt provably came from a REAL enrolled actor (not a fabricated trend).
Notes: ADR-0058 the opt-in verified tier (roadmap Phase 3): raises the mesh trust bar -- each returned actor receipt is SIGNED by the actor enrolled Ed25519 key, and a verified-receipt-collection@1 admits it only when the attestation verifies against the enrolled mesh-actor-keys.json allowlist. meshVerifiedTier.mjs REUSES the ADR-0016 acg-provenance engine (signBundle/verifyWitnessAttestation) -- no new crypto: attestReturnedReceipt signs the exact receipt; validateVerifiedCollection requires the underlying LBA-REQ-076 collection to validate + binds to it by digest + requires every collected receipt to carry a valid attestation from its declared enrolled actor. Fails closed on unsigned/forged-receipt/un-enrolled-actor/wrong-key/not-declared-actor/orphan-attestation/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). Committed enrolled PUBLIC keys + verified collection re-verify offline (private keys never committed). .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml runs the opt-in verified-tier step between the fan-out + the fulfillment gate. Gate mesh-verified-tier-attested. Opt-in + additive: plain fan-out still works; enrolling an actor is publishing its public key.

Requirement: The system shall admit a verified mesh-actor attestation only when it carries an inclusion proof against a transparency-log tree head signed by the enrolled log key -- so a fail-closed gate proves the mesh receipts are enrolled-signed AND publicly auditable (append-only, tamper-evident).
Notes: ADR-0059 transparency-log the mesh-actor attestations (roadmap Phase 3): completes the trust story -- enrolled-signed (LBA-REQ-077) AND publicly auditable. meshTransparency.mjs REUSES the ADR-0022 acg-transparency engine (recordRelease/verifyReleaseInclusion/verifySignedTreeHead, RFC-6962 Merkle) -- no new log crypto: each verified-tier attestation is recorded into a signed Merkle tree; a logged-verified-collection@1 binds to the LBA-REQ-077 verified collection by digest + requires the tree head to verify against the enrolled log key + every attestation to carry an inclusion proof against that signed root. Fails closed on unsigned/wrong-key-tree-head/missing-or-non-reconstructing-proof/tree-size-mismatch/binding-mismatch/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). Committed enrolled log PUBLIC key + logged collection re-verify offline (private key never committed). .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml runs the transparency step after the verified tier + before the fulfillment gate. Gate mesh-attestations-transparency-logged. Verify-before-consume requires BOTH the actor witness signature + a transparency inclusion proof.

Requirement: The system shall admit the mesh transparency log's current tree head only when a consistency proof proves it contains an earlier signed tree head unchanged -- so a fail-closed gate proves the log is APPEND-ONLY (no logged attestation removed or rewritten as it grew).
Notes: ADR-0060 the append-only consistency proof (roadmap Phase 3): closes the append-only claim of LBA-REQ-078 -- inclusion proves an attestation IS in the log, consistency proves the log only GROWS. meshLogHistory.mjs REUSES the ADR-0022 acg-transparency engine (signTreeHead/consistencyProof/verifyConsistency, RFC-6962) -- no new crypto: a logged-collection-history@1 binds an earlier + the current signed tree head + a consistency proof over the real attestation leaves. validateHistory requires both heads to verify against the enrolled log key + the log to have strictly grown + the consistency proof to prove append-only extension + the current head to match the committed LBA-REQ-078 log by Merkle root + size. Fails closed on unsigned/wrong-key-head/non-growing-or-shrinking/bad-consistency-proof/wrong-current-root/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). Committed enrolled log PUBLIC key + history re-verify offline (private key never committed). .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml runs the append-only step. Gate mesh-log-append-only. Inclusion (078) + consistency (079) = the full RFC-6962 transparency guarantee for the mesh.

Requirement: The system shall decide a mesh run FULLY ATTESTED only when its fulfillment, cross-plane parity, verified-tier signatures, transparency inclusion, and append-only proof all hold and name the SAME run identity -- so a fail-closed gate gives a consumer ONE verdict to trust a mesh run end-to-end.
Notes: ADR-0061 the composite mesh-run-attested decision (roadmap Phase 3): the integration capstone -- ONE fail-closed verdict a consumer checks to trust a mesh run end-to-end. meshAttested.mjs decideAttested REUSES every sub-verifier (decideFulfillment 073 + validateReceipt parity 072 + validateVerifiedCollection 077 + validateLoggedCollection 078 + validateHistory 079) with NO new proof logic; a run is attested iff all five gates pass AND all layers name the SAME run identity (cross-proof identity binding). A mesh-run-attested@1 receipt records the gate booleans + shared identity + verdict; validateReceipt re-derives from the committed source receipts (currency). Fails closed on any failing sub-proof / identity-mismatch / stale-gates / verdict-contradiction / tampered-digest (selftest 7/7, one break per sub-proof). Mirrors the composite-release-decision LBA-REQ-071. .github/workflows/mesh-run.yml runs the capstone step last. Gate mesh-run-attested. The mesh subsystem (072-080) is complete.

Requirement: The system shall prove cross-plane VI Analyzer performance parity by validating that a LINUX and a WIN VI Analyzer run share the same benchmark identity and deterministic resultHash, so a fail-closed gate proves the planes ran the SAME benchmark and their run times are comparable performance witnesses.
Notes: ADR-0062 cross-plane VI Analyzer performance parity (roadmap Phase 2): the 2nd benchmark family in the parity suite after launch (LBA-REQ-072). viAnalyzerParity.mjs REUSES the LBA-REQ-072 engine core (launchIdentity/trendOk/decideParity/planeSummary/performanceWitness) via a trendFromEvidence adapter over the real committed vi-analyzer-trend-live-evidence@1 captures (LINUX+WIN, 6 LabVIEWCLI RunVIAnalyzer runs of LabVIEWCLIExampleProject -> 69 tests each). Identity {viAnalyzerMs, vi-analyzer-labviewcli-example, n}. Proves the parity engine is benchmark-generic (not launch-specific). Complements + folds in LBA-REQ-043 (cross-plane VI Analyzer determinism/resultHash): parity-proven only when the planes share BOTH the identity (comparable timing) AND the deterministic resultHash (same answer). Fails closed on identity-mismatch/non-cross-plane/differing-resultHash/invalid-trend/tampered-digest (selftest 7/7). Committed receipt re-derives byte-stably from the two evidence captures (currency). Gate cross-plane-vi-analyzer-parity. The benchmark suite now has 2 families; mass-compile/unit-test parity is a new adapter once real 2-plane timing exists.
